instruction: We represent Kateix Dental Partners, Inc., the buyer in its stock purchase from Laleis Dental Holdings, LLC. Kateix will also receive services under a transition services agreement and is the maker of the seller note. Please review all eight documents in the folder and prepare a memo to me. For each issue, give its location (document and section), explain why it matters for Kateix, and recommend a fix.

rubric.text: The response concludes that Buyer's Notice of Disagreement, delivered May 22, 2026, came after the 45-day window, which closed on May 14, 2026 (45 days from the March 30, 2026 delivery of the Closing Statement), so Seller can treat the Closing Statement as final and binding. It identifies the location as SPA Section 2.4(b) or Side Letter Recital B. It explains why this matters to the client and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the TSA lets Seller assign the TSA, or delegate the services (including billing and patient-records services), to any person without Buyer's consent, while Buyer needs Seller's consent to assign. It identifies the location as TSA Section 12.3. It explains why this matters to the client and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that because the indemnity escrow is Buyer's sole source of recovery for General Representation breaches and is released nine months after Closing (December 2, 2026), the 18-month survival period is effectively cut to nine months. It identifies the location as SPA Section 9.6, SPA Section 9.1 or Escrow Agreement Section 4.2. It explains why this matters to the client and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the stock sale triggered Pellucid Dental Benefits Network's right to consent to a change of control, and that this consent was neither obtained at Closing nor covered by any SPA covenant, since the SPA addresses only landlord consents. It identifies the location as Disclosure Schedule 4.5(b) or SPA Section 6.4. It explains why this matters to the client and recommends a fix.

The response concludes that the TSA liability cap carve-out for Section 8.2 obligations leaves uncapped an indemnity that only Buyer gives, and that this indemnity covers all third-party claims relating to the Services, including claims caused by Seller's own work, so Buyer's exposure under it is unlimited. It identifies the location as TSA Section 9.1 or Section 8.2. It explains why this matters to the client and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Closing Date was March 2, 2026.
The response is written as a memo addressed to the supervising partner and presents each issue separately.
The response claims that Buyer's May 22, 2026 Notice of Disagreement was delivered on time under SPA Section 2.4(b).
The response claims that SPA Section 11.6 restricts Seller's assignment of the TSA.
